newsitem.title: USA: UAW members ratify new UAW-Chrysler pact.
newsitem.headline: UAW members ratify new UAW-Chrysler pact.

text.p: United Auto Workers members at Chrysler Corp have voted to ratify new three-year agreements covering hourly and salaried workers, said UAW president Stephen Yokich and vice president Jack Laskowski, director of the UAW-Chrysler Department.
The ballot count revealed that 73 percent voted in favor of the pact.

Highlights of the new agreement include expanded job security protections, which proide a guaranteed minimum employment floor of 95 percent of current covered jobs, incentives for insourcing work and creating new jobs and disincentives on outsourcing.

Wages and incomes are increased through an up-front, lump-sum payment of $2,000 per covered employee, followed by three percent general base wage increases in the second and third year of the agreement, cost-of-living allowance protection, and Christmas bonuses of up to $600 each.
The successor agreement replaces a pact that expired September 14.
Under the agreement, Chrysler will make tuition assistance payments of up to $1,000 per year for dependent children enrolled in college and other approved post-secondary education and training.
Among other gains, Veterans Day will become a paid holiday in the third year of the agreement, health care benefits are enhanced and group insurance benefits improved.
The contract covers about 66,000 UAW-represented hourly workers and 6,000 UAW-represented salaried workers at Chrysler in the United States.
UAW spokesmen were not immediately available to provide further information.
